title: Israel kills senior Hezbollah commander Fuad Shukr in Beirut strike
body:
On the evening of 30 July 2024 an Israeli airstrike hit a stronghold in Beirut's southern suburbs, an area that houses Hezbollah's headquarters. The Israeli military said it had killed Fuad Shukr, which it described as Hezbollah's most senior military commander, in the rare strike on the Lebanese capital. The Israel Defense Forces said Shukr was an adviser to Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah on wartime operations.

Israeli officials tied Shukr to the rocket attack on the Golan Heights town of Majdal Shams on 27 July 2024, which killed 12 children and teenagers, and to earlier rocket strikes on northern Israel. Hezbollah denied involvement in the Majdal Shams attack. Defense Minister Yoav Gallant said "Hezbollah crossed a red line" and that Shukr had the blood of many Israelis on his hands. An Israeli official told CBS News that Israel notified the United States beforehand.

Lebanon's health ministry, in figures relayed by Agence France-Presse, said one female civilian was killed and 68 civilians were injured, five of them critically. Hezbollah's Al-Manar television reported 17 wounded taken to Bahman Hospital and 14 to Rasoul Aazam hospital. Nasrallah posted that the attempt had failed at first, but on 31 July Hezbollah said it was searching for Shukr's body. Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the strike on a residential building, and Hamas also denounced it. The strike came hours before the killing of Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran.
